# DIY: Assessing the Correctness of Natural Language to SQL Systems

## Research question

Plausible answers can conceal an incorrect mapping from a natural-language request to SQL, especially when users cannot inspect SQL directly.

## Method

DIY wraps RAT-SQL with editable question-to-query mappings and a sandbox containing typically five sampled rows per relevant table. Sampling seeks illustrative positive and negative cases for supported query constructs. Users inspect stepwise natural-language/table explanations, alter sample rows to test behavior, or change mappings before applying the revised query to the original database.

## Evaluation

An exploratory remote study recruits 12 employees from one technology company. Participants receive a tutorial, attempt eight curated tasks with four correct and four erroneous initial responses, and think aloud while an experimenter can probe or assist. The study reports qualitative observations and a System Usability Scale score, without a comparison condition or aggregate task-correction accuracy.

## What the results support

Participants used inspection, sample-data manipulation and mapping changes as distinct debugging strategies. Mean SUS is 65.42. Six participants noticed the ambiguity of since 1980, but only two changed the greater-than mapping. Several confused answers on the sample with those on the full database.

## Limits and qualifications

Small, curated, assisted sessions do not establish comparative efficiency or calibrated trust. Sample construction is incomplete for HAVING, set operations, nested queries and several functions/operators; query explanations have separate coverage. New mappings are restricted by the original interpretation. Successful sample checks do not certify full-data correctness or resolve absent information.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Adjacent evidence for human verification and interpretation repair, including the gap between noticing ambiguity and acting on it. It does not evaluate an autonomous clarification policy, answerability classifier or refusal behavior.
